meta.name: Health Wallet Curated Interaction Rules
meta.description: A small, curated set of well-documented drug-drug interactions used by the Health Wallet rules engine. This is NOT a complete clinical drug interaction database. It must be replaced with a licensed/validated source (e.g. a maintained DrugBank, RxNav/RxNorm interaction API, or a national formulary feed) before any clinical use. Rules are keyed by normalized generic ingredient names.

sources.title: US FDA structured product labeling / medication guides

meta.disclaimer: Informational only. Requires professional review. Never start, stop or change a medicine based on this output.

interactions.effect: Markedly increased risk of serious gastrointestinal and other bleeding.
interactions.mechanism: NSAID-induced platelet inhibition and gastric mucosal injury, added to warfarin's anticoagulant effect.
interactions.management: Avoid the combination where possible; if unavoidable, use gastroprotection and close INR/monitoring per clinician.

interactions.mechanism: Additive haemostatic impairment (platelet inhibition plus anticoagulation).
interactions.management: Only under explicit clinical indication with monitoring.

interactions.mechanism: NSAID platelet effects plus possible CYP2C9 interaction.
interactions.management: Avoid; choose alternative analgesia after clinical review.

interactions.effect: Significant increase in INR / bleeding risk.
interactions.mechanism: Inhibition of CYP2C9 metabolism of warfarin (S-enantiomer).
interactions.management: Anticipate dose adjustment and frequent INR monitoring.

interactions.mechanism: Altered warfarin metabolism and gut flora vitamin K production.
interactions.management: Monitor INR during and after the course.
Monitor INR closely; adjust per clinician.

interactions.mechanism: Additive potassium retention (ACE inhibitor plus potassium-sparing diuretic).
interactions.management: Monitor potassium and renal function; use with clinical oversight.
Monitor serum potassium; avoid unless supervised.

interactions.effect: Reduced blood-pressure control and risk of renal impairment.
interactions.mechanism: NSAID inhibition of prostaglandins reducing renal perfusion.
interactions.management: Use the lowest effective NSAID dose, hydrate, monitor BP and renal function.

interactions.effect: Reduced cardioprotective effect of low-dose aspirin; increased GI bleeding.
interactions.management: Separate dosing timing or choose another analgesic after review.
Consider a different proton-pump inhibitor (e.g. pantoprazole) after review.
Frequently intentional (dual antiplatelet therapy) - confirm clinical plan and monitor for bleeding.
Limit simvastatin dose and monitor for muscle symptoms.

interactions.effect: Possible increased statin exposure and muscle-related effects.
interactions.management: Monitor for muscle pain; review statin choice if symptomatic.

interactions.effect: Reduced levothyroxine absorption, possibly raising TSH.
interactions.management: Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach; recheck thyroid function.
Separate administration by several hours; recheck thyroid function.

interactions.effect: First-dose hypotension and renal function changes.
interactions.management: Monitor BP and renal function, especially on initiation.
